milestone: Alpha 1.72 protocol privacy review; urgent fix eligible for earlier publication
status: prepared source fix; not deployed or a completed security milestone
finding: The production full/delta world broadcast encoded each shared player snapshot identically for owner and nearby peers. A two-player regression reproduced another player's Gold, XP and skill/talent allocation fields in the actual decoded full protobuf envelope. Inventory, EP and account data were already excluded from these snapshots; quests already travel separately and were not reproduced as a current broadcast leak.
fix: Both full and delta encoding now use the bound recipient's character ID. Remote player messages omit Gold, XP/next-level progress, unspent skill/talent points, unlocked skill/talent lists, rune/rank maps and any quest details supplied by future snapshot changes. Encoding does not mutate shared actor snapshots or the owner's message.
preserved: Owner progression, visible identity/spec, equipment/appearance, combat/animation fields and public non-player actors/loot retain their existing behavior. No schema, currency, saves, progression, gameplay balance or private quest-update route changes.

checks.broadcast: Actual production broadcastState builds and queues protobuf full and delta messages for two bound synthetic clients. Each receives its own progression and no peer progression; both retain visible equipment/health/level. An unchanged public actor ensures the second pass exercises the delta path.
checks.encoding: Remote and unidentified recipients receive no progression, including a supplied quest. Owner output remains protobuf-equal before and after peer encoding; nil input and public loot are preserved.
checks.baselineFailure: The regression failed on the unfiltered production broadcast with round0 leaked another player's progression to private-a. Initial fixture compilation/world-background/quest-route corrections are not claimed as discovered production failures.

limits: Queued production-serializer checks are not authenticated socket/private-message coverage or a complete visibility/authorization review.
This fix can ship independently before the full1.72 milestone; its publication still requires aligned release defaults/notes, exact-source CI and public acceptance.
Other protocol movement/cast, admission, event and secret-exposure boundaries remain unfinished.
